text:
Sam H.: Heads-up — after the staging deploy (commit abc123) INT8 perf on convo workloads jumped: p95 token latency ~40% higher vs yesterday. Repro on a100 and our local dev nodes.

Luca M.: ugh. Which workload? long sequences or short chat paths?

Sam H.: Mostly chat (seq_len ~256, kv cache warm). Batch sizes 4-12. Quick profiling shows extra time in dequant + generic matmul path. Flamegraph snippet: `dequant_kernel -> generic_gemm -> kv_merge` dominates.

Priya S.: Can you paste the kernel selection log? I remember a kernel-routing tweak landed in PR #3409 last night.

Sam H.: Pasted below from runtime debug logs (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-17T21:04:12Z] request id=... model=gpt-like int8 profile
selected_kernel: generic_dequant_gemm (cost=12.1)
alt_kernel: fused_int8_attention (cost=14.5)
note: kv_cache_hit=true seq=256 batch=8
```

Sam H.: The cost model is picking generic_dequant_gemm even when fused_int8_attention would have been faster in practice (because it ignored KV cache reuse of packed weights). That smells like the PR that changed the kernel cost estimator.

Deniz K.: I ran a quick bisect across the last 6 merges. PRs 3403 and 3409 were suspects. Disabling the new estimator in staging restores previous numbers.

Luca M.: Good catch. Does CI perf suite also fail?

Sam H.: Yes — perf CI (nightly) shows the same regression on x86 and a100 images. Job link: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/18512 (restricted).

infra-bot: Alert: perf-nightly job 18512 regression +23% p95 for int8-chat-batch. See artifacts.

Priya S.: If the estimator underestimated the benefit of packed fused kernels when kv_cache==true, we need either a quick revert or a targeted patch. Canary rollout is currently blocked (slo-check failed).

Sam H.: Repro script attached (run on a100):
```
python tools/run_perf.py --model gpt-like --dtype int8 --seq 256 --batch 8 --kv-warm
```

Luca M.: Bisect notes: PR 3409 modified kernel selector to use `avg_latency` measured from microbenchmarks, but the microbenchmarks didn't simulate KV cache reuse: packed kernels have init cost amortized across tokens. The estimator treats per-op latency for one-shot runs, so selection flips to generic path for shorter micro runs.

Priya S.: So it's a measurement bias. Fixes: 1) revert PR 3409 (fast) 2) update estimator to consider amortized init cost and kv_cache hit factor (longer-lasting sessions) (slow but correct) 3) add CI microbench that simulates KV-warm steady-state.

Sam H.: Proposing revert + followup: open PR to revert 3409 and then another PR to improve estimator and add CI case. Any objections?

Deniz K.: +1 for revert. I'll draft the revert PR and link perf numbers. Also want to add a runtime feature flag so we can toggle the new estimator without revert in future.

Luca M.: Fine with revert. For followup estimator change: we should add a term for amortized kernel init: cost = measured_latency + init_cost / (expected_tokens). Also include kv_cache boolean multiplier. I can sketch the math.

Priya S.: I'll update the rollout playbook: when kernel-selector changes land, run perf suite with kv-warm scenarios and scaled batch sizes. Add test coverage.

Sam H.: Creating incident ticket and will block canary until revert lands. Ticket: INF-2173.

deploy-bot: Revert PR created: #3421 reverting PR 3409 — awaiting reviews.

Deniz K.: Ran quick local with revert applied — p95 back to baseline within noise (~2%). Attaching before/after numbers in artifacts.

Luca M.: After revert we should still merge an improved estimator. I'll own the design doc. TL;DR: simulate steady-state in microbench, incorporate kv_cache factor, prefer fused kernels when init amortization threshold met.

Priya S.: Thanks everyone. Sam — can you keep the canary blocked and mark INF-2173 status as "mitigated" once revert merges?

Sam H.: Yep. Will monitor perf-nightly and unfreeze canary after two successful runs.

Luca M.: One more note: there are 2 edge cases for int4/fp8 profiles where dequant path behaves differently. We'll run quick regressions for those too after revert.

Sam H.: Thanks. Quick checklist: revert PR, update rollout playbook, add kv-warm microbench to CI, design doc for estimator.

Deniz K.: On it.

Priya S.: :thumbsup:
